questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to find a University in a country with beautiful nature and a lot of outdoor activities such as hiking and skiing.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit tricky at times since you have to use many different web sites, however I always found good help by writing a mail to somebody who new something about the different processes.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had an intro night for international student with pizza afterwards. It was a good opourtunity to meet other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty hard. Vancouver is expensive. I found other danes going to Vancouver and we shared an AirBnB. I can recommend renting an AirBnB if it's not too expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a bit harder to meet up with other students. I think living on campus makes that a lot easier.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit hard to understand at first, but I think KU or UBC arranged a meeting prior to the exchange that explained how to do it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find the courses and short course description and then you register somewhere else, I think it was on a website called workday.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could mail somebody from UBC. I did that and they were very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I was succesfull in registering, but I only got 4 out of 8 or 10 subjects. However I only needed 4 so it was fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use a good amount of time looking into the different courses, your exchange will be more fun if you like the courses you end up taking.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was interesting but not on a very high level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were pretty easy. I took level 300 courses (third year courses). I didn't put too much effort and still got good grades, but I guess it depends a lot on the individual course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of my courses were small lectures and some teachers learned my name because the class was small and you some times get graded on participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Culture, Power & Politics 
- Microbes and Society
- Sex and Gender in the Economy 
- The History of Modern Medicine

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of them were very interesting and I had great professors.
I think for publiv health I think it was very interesting learning more about Microbes and Society.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Not many. Small things the apartment lacked and eating a lot out for lunch on campus.
Tax! They dont write the tax on the price of the product, sp you won't see the full price before you are at the cashier, tax is around 12%.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was a bit more expensive then expected but probably the same as in Denmark. Eating out is less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I can recommend the VOC (outdoor club). You pay 50$ to be a member and then you can rent gear for free with a deposit. They also make great trips. You can also sign up for the intermurals, which is all kind of different sports leagues and you join a team.

UBC also have free drop in sport every weekday. It could be volley, futsal, basketball etc..

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, there a A LOT of different clubs. See above for sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you like skiing or snowboarding get an Epic pass for Whistler. Whislter is a great and big ski resort only 2 hours by bus from UBC. It's easy to get there, I sometimes went just for one day. You have to buy it many months before your semester starts, I would say 5 months because they get sold it. It's around 4200 dkk for the whole season at is very worth it. It's the place to be skiing in the area.

It is also possible to ski on Cypress, Seymore and Grouse mountain but these are very small resorts with only a couple of lift.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking or skiing, go to Vancouver Island. Go thrift shopping, it is really good in Vancouver when you get away from downtown.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, canadians are very nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask them how they are doing. I found it easy to just chat a bit with people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They were a lot younger then me, not that it was a big challenge.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very nice!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Remember why you wanted to go on exchange and remember it when you get there. You don't have to go out every weekend if you would rather be hiking or doing other things and vice versa. Make plans that you wanna do and ask if anybody wants to join, someone is almost always up for it.
2. Get a student Epic pass for Whistler!
3. Pressure yourself to socialize in the beginning. A little effort pays of easily.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to have fun:)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The lovely people, the nature and skiing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time flies and there are a lot of cool things to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I can really recommend UBC!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
